title: AdaptEvolve: Improving Efficiency of Evolutionary AI Agents through Adaptive Model Selection

mechanism.domainTask: Evolutionary code refinement with adaptive LLM routing
mechanism.populationDetail: Two persistent islands are configured; candidates are refined within an OpenEvolve-style population and a MAP-Elites-style archive, with migration-related configuration.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The paper explicitly calls the archive MAP-Elites style and gives descriptor dimensions pass rate and complexity; prior high-scoring generations are reused as exemplars.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Population and archive mechanics are inherited from the base framework and are less fully specified than the routing mechanism.
mechanism.generationDetail: A candidate \(x_i\) from \(P_t\) is passed to a mutation call and rewritten into the next code generation; no localized patch protocol is described.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Pass-rate outcomes and confidence features are used to train or update the router and determine whether to stay with the small model or escalate.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The parent-selection rule for \(x_i\) is not exposed clearly; MAP-Elites archive entries are contextual references rather than additional true parents.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/AdaptEvolve Improving Efficiency of Evolutionary AI Agents through Adaptive Model Selection.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The paper's core contribution is confidence-driven adaptive routing between two models. The survey also cites it as a multi-objective example, although the per-candidate benchmark signal is primarily scalar/binary; population, parent-selection, and prompt details are partly inherited from OpenEvolve.
